hypotheses.author: model
hypotheses.claim: Normalization gains can amplify small parameter changes into network-wide changes in residual-stream scaling and attention calibration. Freezing these gains while leaving embeddings and all attention/MLP matrices trainable should preserve useful adaptation better than reducing every parameter's learning rate further. At lr 3e-5, I predict 0.8 points less forgetting than no mitigation and a legal perplexity ratio of 0.750–0.754. Run seeds 0 and 1. A retention improvement with unchanged legal learning would support normalization drift as a specific residual interference pathway; worse legal perplexity would instead indicate that normalization plasticity contributes materially to adaptation.
